decontamination_notes: Real Host-header validation hardening from pallets/werkzeug PR #3236 ('validate host port', https://github.com/pallets/werkzeug/pull/3236), merged 2026-08-12 -- after the training cutoffs of the models evaluated here (e.g. Opus 5, May 2026), so the specific fix is not in their training data (decontaminated: true), with upstream_merged recorded as proof. host_is_trusted() (werkzeug/sansio/utils.py) decides whether a request's Host header matches the trusted-host allowlist. It strips the port before comparing but never validates it, so a Host header with a malformed or out-of-range port (:0, :99999, a leading-zero port) is still treated as trusted -- weakening Host-header validation, which guards against Host-header injection, cache poisoning, and bad absolute-URL construction. The fix captures the port in the host regex (requiring [1-9][0-9]{,4}) and range-checks it (1..65535), returning False for an invalid port. werkzeug is pure Python; its package __init__ imports MarkupSafe, so MarkupSafe is vendored into repo/_vendor (built for the sandbox's linux-amd64) and hidden tests run offline with PYTHONPATH=src:_vendor on the base image. Repo sliced at the PR base commit (src/, 21.9k LOC; host_is_trusted with the un-validated port); BSD-3-Clause LICENSE preserved. Coverage floor: 3 fail_to_pass (a zero port, an out-of-range port, and a leading-zero port are each wrongly trusted at base and rejected after the fix) plus a 3-check regression guard (a valid port is trusted, no port is trusted, an untrusted host is rejected).
